pr_title: R: Fix protection errors for relational API
pr_body:
Closes #6465.

This adds a tiny change to the vendored cpp11 code, we should eventually upstream it to take advantage of future updates.

issue_context.title: R: Protection error in relational API
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

The relational API appears to crash randomly in unexpected ways, looking very much like a protection error. I have managed to extract a simple-ish minimal reproducible example.

Disabling/removing each of the components labeled "necessary", as well as enabling (???) the `gc()` in the loop, appears to hide the error.

### To Reproduce

``` r
df <- data.frame(a = integer(0))
# Necessary:
class(df) <- c("tbl", "data.frame")

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

# Simple projection
exprs <- list(duckdb:::expr_reference("a"))
rel <- duckdb:::rel_from_df(con, df)
# Necessary: storing out_rel in a variable, inlining the variable fixes the problem?
out_rel <- duckdb:::rel_project(rel, exprs)
sp <- duckdb:::rel_to_altrep(out_rel)
rm(out_rel)

# Necessary:
rm(rel)

# Necessary (2x):
gc()
#>           used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) limit (Mb) max used (Mb)
#> Ncells  889265 47.5    1426247 76.2         NA  1426247 76.2
#> Vcells 1612820 12.4    8388608 64.0      24576  2927421 22.4
gc()
#>           used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) limit (Mb) max used (Mb)
#> Ncells  889655 47.6    1426247 76.2         NA  1426247 76.2
#> Vcells 1613699 12.4    8388608 64.0      24576  2927421 22.4

# Crashes after 10-300 iterations:
for (i in 1:1000) {
  message(i)
  y_rel <- duckdb:::rel_from_altrep_df(sp)
  duckdb:::rapi_rel_to_df(y_rel)

  # gc() # Error disappears if we do a gc() in each iteration (???)
}
```

review_comments: Looks good, but can't we do the list wrapping in make_external_prot, too?
Does this mean passing two arguments to `make_external_prot()`, or just inlining the `prot` variable?
I was thinking of the latter but not sure if it still shows the desired behaviour
I suspect it would, the temporary `list` won't be destroyed for the duration of the `make_external()`call, and hece will remain protected. We can try in a second iteration.
